summary.text: A 34-year-old HIV-positive woman with a CD4 count of 24 cells/µL who was not on HAART presented with confusion and ataxia. Examination showed nystagmus, severe dysarthria and a broad-based gait. She had a history of alcohol abuse, and Wernicke encephalopathy was considered and treated with thiamine.

MRI showed high signal on T2-weighted and FLAIR sequences in the left cerebellar hemisphere, pons and midbrain without restricted diffusion, mass effect or enhancement. CSF culture showed no growth and the JC virus PCR was positive. The patient deteriorated in the ward and subsequently demised.

summary.text: A 34-year-old HIV-positive man on HAART with a CD4 count of 30 cells/µL presented with a 1-month history of cerebellar ataxia. CT showed hypodensity in the left cerebellar hemisphere and generalised cerebral atrophy; MRI showed multiple T2 high-signal changes in the pons and right cerebellar hemisphere with some enhancement and no restriction on DWI.
